202B.11 / CHAPTER 11 OF 11

How to trade the swing

How do you shape a 3-9 day trade around the expected demand wave?

11 chapters with worked investigations

01Price structure02Base & repricing03Supply zones04Demand & absorption05Holder rotation06Expansion & pullback07Continuation vs distribution08Swing lifecycle09Retracement references: 0.5 & 0.61810Comprehensive swing check11How to trade the swing

01Definition

Assess the wave, then build the container: estimate how large demand could become and when it could arrive, enter early before the expected repricing, and sell into the rise. A swing allows pressure to develop over days within a defined frame and time window.

02Why it matters

The same thesis can offer an early entry or a late chase. Structure, absorption and holder behavior help judge which part of the expected wave is still available; the trade must fit that wave rather than an indefinite hope of recovery.

03What to check

  • Wave and entry: use the comprehensive swing check to identify the demand source, plausible scale and arrival window. Define an early-entry condition using structure, absorption and holder behavior before the expected repricing.
  • Size and hold: fit exposure to usable liquidity, supply risk and uncertainty. Allow pressure to build only while the thesis, demand engine and ownership conditions remain intact.
  • Exit and failure: plan where or when to sell into the rise. Define the thesis break, overwhelming distribution, and expiry of the time window that end the trade.

04Healthy / Dangerous

Healthy

Entry precedes expected demand, position size fits an executable exit, and a quiet buildup remains inside the planned window with its conditions intact. Profit-taking captures the rise as the wave arrives.

Dangerous

Entry chases a completed burst, price stability hides stranded holders, or the catalyst disappears while insiders distribute. The trader repeatedly extends the window instead of recognizing failure.

05Beginner mistake

Turning a failed snipe into a swing, mistaking patience for evidence, or using a later recovery to validate a trade whose original frame already failed.

06Takeaway

Enter early and sell into the rise. A swing gives demand more time to build than a snipe, but still requires a defined frame, a time window, and conditions for failure.

Assess the wave → build the container → enter early → allow demand to develop → sell into the rise.

Wave / entry / size / hold / exit / failure.

Frame and time define success; a later recovery cannot rescue an already invalidated trade.

ILLUSTRATIVE · NOT A LIVE TOKEN

See the idea

  1. 01

    Wave and entry: a narrative is spreading through new creator audiences. Plan a seven-day swing: entry region 1.00-1.10 before broad repricing, expected wave 1.50-1.80. Enter only if the base holds, selling is absorbed and the comprehensive checks support continued outreach.

  2. 02

    Size and hold: choose exposure whose current sell quote fits the allowed cost. Hold a quiet day 2 only while the 1.00 base, outreach and ownership conditions remain intact. Fresh independent buying must broaden by the end of day 3; otherwise exit.

  3. 03

    Capture or fail: sell half into 1.50-1.60, then exit the remainder by 1.80, on fading demand, or at day 7, whichever comes first. Exit earlier if the base fails without recovery or linked selling overwhelms buyers. These invented regions demonstrate a plan, not universal targets.

WORKED INVESTIGATION · ILLUSTRATIVE

Work through the evidence

Mechanism and worked case

Illustrative narrative swing: enter in 1.00-1.10 as creators and KOLs reach fresh audiences, after comprehensive checks and absorbed selling support the base. Expect 1.50-1.80 inside seven days. A quiet day 2 fits only while the 1.00 base, outreach and ownership remain intact; fresh independent buying must broaden by the end of day 3. At 1.55 on day 4, sell half into the rise. Exit the remainder by 1.80, on fading demand, or at day 7, whichever comes first. Exit earlier for an unrecovered base failure, overwhelming linked selling or a missed day-three demand condition. A product-led variation can use a confirmed day-seven release and its own deadline; cancellation invalidates that demand source. All prices and windows are invented teaching choices.

How to investigate it

Write the demand source, plausible wave size and expected arrival time before choosing entry. Use the earlier structure and absorption chapters to define an early entry rather than chase the run. Specify exposure against liquidity, supply risk and uncertainty; conditions for holding through a quiet buildup; profit-taking into the rise; and thesis, distribution or time exits. Reassess observed demand inside that frame without repeatedly moving the deadline.

Check your reasoning — answered

The base still holds on day 3, but outreach has stopped and independent buying has not broadened by the end of that day. Should you wait until day 7 because the price target is unchanged? No. The earlier demand condition failed. The seven-day limit is a maximum, not a reason to ignore an earlier invalidation.

Try it on a token

See it in Meme Fast → Swing

Use sampled flow and price response in Inspect to assess absorption and selling. Verify catalyst timing and execution quotes separately; Meme Fast does not provide a complete live tape or guarantee exit capacity.

Go deeper

Use 202B.1-9 for structure, bases, supply zones, absorption, holder rotation, pullbacks and distribution. These refine timing after the demand thesis is assessed; retracement levels alone do not create buyers. The expected low and high are entry and exit regions, not exact extrema known in advance. A quiet period can fit a swing if the demand source, ownership conditions and catalyst remain intact inside the chosen 3-9 day window. It is failure when necessary conditions break or the required demand does not arrive by the predefined deadline. Profit-taking can be staged into the rise; do not substitute a fixed target for observing whether the demand engine is fading. On established multi-venue tokens, check broader market conditions and actual venue depth alongside the local thesis. Open interest and funding apply only where derivatives exist; a CEX listing does not automatically establish liquidity or safety. A new opportunity after failure needs a new assessment rather than a retrospective extension of the original trade.
